reason: Seiko Transistor wall clock in an attractive mid-century gold diamond case; known maker with modest collector interest, value depends on working order.
findings: Gold-tone diamond-shaped wall clock with engraved scroll panels in each corner and small brass-coloured corner posts. Dial reads 'SEIKO' at 12 and 'TRANSISTOR' at 6, both clearly legible, which supports the title. No model number, serial, date code or movement markings visible (back and movement not photographed). A handwritten price sticker sits on the dial lower left (illegible). The 40 x 40 cm size claim cannot be checked from the photo.
condition: Hands all present; crystal looks clear with some reflections and minor marks; gold case finish looks bright with no obvious loss in the photo. Working order unknown (battery transistor movement not shown, no battery or back view).
rescore_note: Dial legibly reads SEIKO TRANSISTOR and the gold diamond case looks clean, but these 1960s-70s battery clocks were mass produced and sell modestly even when running; working order is unknown (no back or movement shown), so upper end of the $30-80 band (judgement, no live comps this run).
